subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lead-in and Listening 2.4.1: how the SQU Rovers help new students / Listening 2.4.2 and Soundbites: asking for, checking and confirming clarification
outcomes: Understand how the SQU Rovers help new students
Listen to an interview and a conversation for main ideas and details
Use phrases to ask for, check and confirm clarification

tf.s: The SQU Rovers are a team of students who help new students.
tf.why: Yes, they help new students at SQU.

tf.s: Nadia is a third-year student who is a Rover.
Fatma is looking for the library.
tf.why: Fatma is looking for Hall B.

tf.s: A common problem for new students is finding their way around the campus.
tf.why: Right, the campus can be confusing at first.

tf.s: Students who lose their ID cards should go to the Administration Office.
tf.why: Yes, they report it and get a replacement.

tf.s: The placement test finds students' level in English, Maths and IT.
tf.why: Correct, it shows which level they start at.

tf.s: The Rovers tell homesick students that nobody else feels the same.
tf.why: They say everyone goes through the same thing and it will get better.

tf.s: 'Are you with me?' is a phrase for checking clarification.
tf.why: Yes, it checks the listener understands.

tf.s: 'Got it!' is a phrase for asking for clarification.
tf.why: Got it! confirms that you understand.

tf.s: Rovers can only be found in the library.
tf.why: They are at stations such as the cafeteria and in front of the mosque.

boxes.why: She needs to find Hall B.

boxes.q: What does the placement test find?
o: students' level in English, Maths and IT
boxes.why: It places students at the right level.

boxes.q: Where should you go if you lose your ID card?
boxes.why: You report it there and get a new one.
Do you mean...? asks the speaker to explain.

o: I'm not sure I follow you.

boxes.q: How does a new student often feel when far from home?

boxes.why: Rovers wait at stations around the university.

boxes.q: How does the new student in the picture feel?
boxes.why: He is new and does not know his way.

hunt.q: Team that helps new SQU students
Where to report a lost ID

o: a third-year student who is a Rover
mcq.why: Nadia is an experienced student helper.

mcq.q: Why are new students sometimes upset?
o: they lose their ID cards and are homesick
mcq.why: Lost IDs and homesickness are common problems.

mcq.q: Which three subjects does the placement test cover?
mcq.why: The test finds students' level in these subjects.

mcq.q: Which sentence tells the speaker you need an explanation?
o: I'm not clear what that is.
mcq.why: It tells the speaker you need an explanation.

mcq.q: Your friend gives you directions and you don't follow. What do you say?
o: Sorry, I'm not sure I follow you.

mcq.q: You are explaining a route and want to check your friend understands. What do you say?
o: I'm not clear what that is.
mcq.why: This checks the listener is following.

mcq.q: Your friend explains which door to use and now you understand. What do you say?
o: I'm not sure I follow you.

mcq.q: How do the Rovers help with homesickness?
o: they say everyone goes through the same thing and it will get better
mcq.why: Knowing others feel the same helps.

mcq.q: Why are Rovers placed at stations like the cafeteria and in front of the mosque?
o: new students can find them easily in busy places
mcq.why: Busy, central places make help easy to reach.

mcq.q: Why is asking for clarification a useful skill for new students?
o: it helps them understand information they need instead of getting lost
